question: Issue 688 (https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/issues/688), code at 1e1e1f78 (https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/pull/694). A non-leader thread in ordinary mode calls execve. What takes the leader out of its PTRACE_EVENT_EXIT stop before finish_ordinary_terminal calls getevent, so that getevent returns ESRCH and the Exec edge has no status? Is that EXIT stop the leader's own exit or the exec's zap, and what status would it have reported?
answer:
No signal wakes the leader out of its EXIT stop. The tracer resumes that stop itself with a stale PTRACE_CONT.

1. After the clone event, the tracer single-steps the leader (task.rs:6008 → step_stopped at 5455) and receives a SIGTRAP stop (status 0x57f).
2. The run loop hands that stop to handle_stop_event (task.rs:3154) → handle_signal (3858) → handle_sigtrap. Its default branch at task.rs:3638 calls resume_stopped(task, None), which reaches the PTRACE_CONT at task.rs:5444. The tracer resumes the new non-leader thread first.
3. If the non-leader calls execve before the leader's CONT is issued, de_thread's zap_other_threads sends the leader SIGKILL. That takes the leader out of its tracer-held 0x57f stop with no tracer request, and it enters the EXIT stop (0x6057f).
4. The CONT meant for the 0x57f stop then lands on the EXIT stop and succeeds (rc=0).
5. The leader runs on to exit and becomes a zombie, and de_thread completes. getevent at the leader's TID (tracer.rs:547, unprobed) then gets ESRCH, and the Exec edge raises #688.

The EXIT stop comes from the exec's zap, not from the leader exiting on its own. The leader loops in pause() and never exits by itself. SIGKILL was seen pending while it sat in its trace stop, and the event message is the exec-zap value. The stop would have reported 0, i.e. Exited(0), which is what the tests expect. A raw GETEVENTMSG taken inside the window returned 0 in 5 of 5 cases, and kernel v7.1 exit.c:1100-1101 sets the exec-zap exit code to 0.

The comment's hypothesis, that a timer step advanced the stop, is refuted for all 17 captured instances: no timer or other request reached the leader in the window.

fix_implications:
What the tracer knows at the Exec edge:
- The leader's 0x6057f had already been latched by the notifier before the stale CONT, 3 to 137 µs earlier in 6 of 7 natural instances.
- The Exec edge names the former TID.
- getevent returned ESRCH.

The EXIT payload is then gone from the kernel: the leader is released by de_thread, and the former TID's pidfd gets ECHILD. So the retry loop at the Exec edge (session.retry_after(ExitEventStatusUnavailable)) can never succeed. Every failure stays Pending until the 3 s deadline.

A check before the resume (look at the latched EXIT stop or exit epoch before resume_stopped) narrows the window but cannot close it. SIGKILL can move the tracee from the reported 0x57f stop into the EXIT stop at any moment outside a ptrace request (sched/signal.h:447-449). The kernel also accepts a CONT against whichever trace stop the tracee is in (ptrace.c:193). Run-47 shows the gap can be under 1 µs. So a fence on the resume alone cannot close the window, with or without a retry. It can be closed only by not needing the lost payload.

Option 1: derive the displaced leader's status from the Exec edge.
- Kernel exit.c:1100-1101 sets the exec-zap exit code to 0, and all measurements agree.
- This contradicts the current comment at the Exec edge ("Losing the old EXIT payload cannot authorize a fabricated consuming hook").
- It is only sound when the loss came from a zap. zap_other_threads also sends SIGKILL to a leader already in its own EXIT stop (signal.c:1348 skips only threads with exit_state set). That would lose a real nonzero status with the same observable signature. This comes from reading the source only; it was not measured.
- A safe rule must tell apart an EXIT stop entered from a stop the tracer never released (zap, status 0) from one entered after a tracer resume.

Option 2: reorder the clone path so the leader's post-clone step stop is resumed before the new child is resumed (task.rs:6008 and the run-loop CONT order). An exec by the child could then only zap a running leader, never a leader held in a stop. This narrows the race by construction but does not cover other held stops.
open_questions: Can the exec zap also take a leader out of its own EXIT stop (status N) and lose N? The kernel source suggests yes (the fatal wake applies to any trace stop), but it was not measured. The answer decides whether 'Exec edge + ESRCH => Exited(0)' is sound in general.

Run-47's ordering (-0.7 µs between the CONT and the 0x6057f wait) cannot be resolved with timestamps taken at syscall return. A shared sequence number taken around every ptrace request and every waitid return would settle it.

For the natural failures, the stale CONT's caller (handle_sigtrap at task.rs:3638) is inferred from the same ptrace site (5444) and the same preceding stop kind. The backtrace was captured only in the forced run.

In campaign run 17, postexec_timer_survives_internal_step also failed with 'unexpected ptrace terminal stop: Signal(SIGTRAP)'. That is a different signature, possibly https://github.com/rrnewton/reverie/issues/686. My probes dump only at ESRCH or at the Exec edge, so no timeline was captured for it.

refuted_hypotheses: A synchronous timer step advanced the physical EXIT stop (the comment at tracer.rs:574-576): refuted for all 17 captured instances. No timer tgkill, step or other request reached the leader in the window; the consuming resume is the handle_sigtrap CONT at task.rs:3638 → 5444.
The EXIT stop is the leader's own exit: refuted. The leader loops in pause(); SIGKILL was pending in its trace stop; the event message is 0, the exec-zap value.
A signal wakes the leader out of its EXIT stop: refuted. The EXIT stop persisted 3.2 ms with no signal pending and ended only at the tracer's own CONT.
The leader is always blocked in pause() when the zap arrives: true only in passing runs. In every failing instance the leader was in the tracer-held post-clone SIGTRAP stop (0x57f).
